hub.speaker: Krshia
hub.text: Hrr. My crate. Gone from the storeroom three nights past. Sewers, I think. There are scavenger tracks at the grate behind the fish stalls, and the bars are bent wide.

text_variants.text: Stall closes with the light. Come back at a decent hour, or knock and keep at it. The front of the table is boxed and the good stock went in first. What is left out is cloth and trestles.
You come back. Any word on my crate?
Crate is home. You, I will remember. Yes.
So you went in with your fists and asked your questions after. Loud, that. But the crate is home, and nothing in it rattles loose.
You found it with your own eyes and no knuckles spent. That is sharper than most bring me. Where did you learn to look first?
You sent the Watch to do it for you. Sensible. It came home on a Watch cart, stamps whole. This goes in my ledger, with the debts I owe.
You have the look of someone come to ask a favor. Speak plainly. I have no patience for the other kind.
The inn's order, extended. For the barmaid's sake, and yours. It goes out on the morning cart, with the flour.

options.text: The scavengers dragged it into a cellar. I've seen it myself. (Light)
The inn's order ran short. Extend it, for Lyonette's sake. [Charming Smile]
Just cover the shortfall myself. (2 gold)
You said the necklace was a promise.
I've a few things I don't need. Buying?
What's the story with the inn's order?

options._comment: v0.16 F1 TALK (#308). TRAP: both rows APPEND LAST -- once rags_meeting_settled is held they render VISIBLE-LOCKED, not hidden, so placement is what protects every index-pinned array on this hub.
options.text: The camp south needs winter stores. Move a quiet run for them. [Charming Smile]
Stand the cost of a quiet run south myself. (8 gold)

goblin_run.speaker: Krshia
goblin_run.text: Hrr. South. Grain, salt, hide-thread, and a cart that does not stop where anyone is counting. I will not ask whose hands it ends in. On my books it is wool, and you pay the wool price.

krshia_tribe.speaker: Krshia
krshia_tribe.text: My tribe, yes. Plains east and south of here — many hearths, one name. I am a Gnoll with a stall in Liscor, and the tribe is still mine. The necklace is a promise. I do not take it off.

krshia_tribe_two.speaker: Krshia
krshia_tribe_two.text: That promise, you may ask about when you have known me longer than one crate. Hrr. The wool wants restacking before the rain comes. Hand me the bolt by your elbow.

krshia_plans.speaker: Krshia
krshia_plans.text: So you remembered. Hrr. Then hear a little of it. Every coin this stall clears past its keep goes toward something for the tribes. Something Gnolls have been told we cannot have. We save for it anyway. There is a gathering, some years off. I mean to stand up at it with full hands. That stays between you, me, and the wool.

options.text: Full hands. I'd like to see that.

krshia_plans_two.speaker: Krshia
krshia_plans_two.text: You will, if the city behaves and the thieves stay bored. And you are now a keeper of Silverfang business. For you, the front-of-stall price is the back-of-stall price. Come early on market days. The good stock does not sit past noon.

shop.speaker: Krshia
shop.text: Silverfang goods. Best in Liscor, and I will hear no argument on it. Cheapest at the front, the good stock where a browsing hand drifts. Coin on the counter and it is yours. No discounts, no haggling. I remember faces.

options.text: That Silverfang hunting knife. Good steel. (15 gold)
The wool-lined cloak. The wet gets in, out on the road. (18 gold)
The old charm-cord, friend's price. (4 gold)
That Silverfang hunting knife, friend's price. (13 gold)
The wool-lined cloak, friend's price. (16 gold)
The boiled-leather jerkin, friend's price. (22 gold)
The hunting bow, then. Gnoll-strung, proper draw. (18 gold)

charms.speaker: Krshia
charms.text: The charmed stock costs more because it does more. Wear too much of it at once and it starts to argue with itself, so choose with sense. Coin on the counter, same as the rest.

options.text: That copper ring. Can't hurt. (4 gold)
The handline, for the pond. (4 gold)
The stone-scale, the one under the counter. (35 gold)
That piece under the far cloth. What is it? (18 gold)
That stone with the Pallass stamp on the wrapping. (18 gold)

catalyst_sold.speaker: Krshia
catalyst_sold.text: That one, I do not ask questions about. Silverfang trade brings stranger things than that through Liscor. It came in under the wool two winters back and it has sat under that cloth since. Yours now. Wrap it before you carry it. It hums against tin, yes?

pallass_stone_sold.speaker: Krshia
pallass_stone_sold.text: Guild paper and a Silverfang stone, together — the city won't ask twice. Keep both on you until the Door has done its work.

bought.speaker: Krshia
bought.text: Sold. Wear it and use it. Mending costs extra. Anything else catch your eye?

accepted.speaker: Krshia
accepted.text: Good. Sewer grates, south of here. Start there. Careful of teeth.

thanks.speaker: Krshia
thanks.text: Yes. This is mine. Stamps whole, lid tight. My thanks. Take that corner — it goes behind the counter.

smoothed.speaker: Krshia
smoothed.text: For the barmaid, then. She is prickly, that one, but she works. I have watched her learn it. The order goes out full, and no word of the shortfall reaches Erin from my stall. You speak plainly and you speak for a friend. I respect both. It leaves with the morning cart.

smoothed_paid.speaker: Krshia
smoothed_paid.text: Coin instead of words. Simpler, some days. The order goes out full and Erin hears nothing of the shortfall. We are square, you and I.

wrong_order_recap.speaker: Krshia
wrong_order_recap.text: The inn's shortfall, yes. Smooth it here at my stall, or settle it your own way. Lyonette gets her full order once it is done.

text_variants.text: That's handled on my end. Go tell Lyonette, back at the inn, before Erin hears it from someone else.
